_note: webagents mcp list / mcp add and the chat's /mcp list / /mcp add (2026-09-29): the words, the settings files read, how another app's entry is read, shown, converted (keys to this profile's secrets) and written into an agent. Read by python/tests/cli/test_mcp_import.py and typescript/tests/unit/cli/mcp-import.test.ts; every expected value is written by hand. Key-looking values here are made up and match the SDK's patterns only.

words.heading: MCP servers other apps on this machine use
words.none: No MCP servers in the settings of Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Windsurf.
words.addHint: Add one to an agent: {command}, or /mcp add <name> in the chat.
words.stored: Stored {names} in this profile's secrets; the entry reads them as ${secret:NAME}.
words.restart: The agent connects it the next time it starts.
words.notFound: No MCP server named {name} in other apps' settings; {command} shows them.
words.ambiguous: {name} is in more than one app's settings ({apps}); say which with --from <app>.
words.unknownApp: No app named {app}; use one of {apps}.
words.exists: {agent} already has an MCP server named {name}.
words.keyOnCommandLine: {name} carries what looks like a key in its {field}; move it to env in {app}, then add it again.
words.otherAppReference: {name} uses {reference}, which only {app} fills in; add it by hand with the value in place.
words.cannotEdit: {file} lists its MCP servers in a layout this cannot edit safely. Add these lines under its mcp entry:
words.noAgent: No agent file in {folder}; {command} makes one.
words.manyAgents: More than one agent file in {folder}; name one: {files}.
words.secretsStay: It read {names} from this profile's secrets; they stay stored (`{command}` removes one).
words.cannotRemove: {file} lists its MCP servers in a layout this cannot edit safely; take {name} out of it by hand.
words.restartRemoved: The agent stops using it the next time it starts.

jsonc.about: comments of both kinds and trailing commas go; the same characters inside strings stay
an escaped quote does not end a string
a comment runs to the end of its line only

normalize.about: a command entry keeps its command, arguments, variables and folder
numbers and booleans become text the way JavaScript writes them; null, lists and mappings are dropped
arguments that are not a list are dropped, and a command line in command is then split
a whole command line in command, as Cursor writes it, is split into words
a command line with a quote left open is kept as written
a command line ending in a lone backslash is kept as written
a command with arguments of its own is not split
an empty command falls through to the address
neither a command nor an address
